title: Two isolated machines, no network: each verdict equals the expected verdict

source.abstract: bundle determines INVALID; a consulting verifier returns UNVERIFIABLE on both machines (they agree)

scenario: The same bundle, trust configuration and request on two machines with no network. Each machine's six stable fields are compared with the expected six, not only with each other (A5.1: agreement alone passes a fail-closed consulting verifier).
base: three bundles, one per V1 verdict value

mutations.detail: two hosts, network interfaces down (or egress denied), fresh installs of the same release

choices: The probe's 'optional service' is a revocation view; V1 consults none. Bundles chosen to cover each V1 verdict value (the probe's FailClosed trace is an INVALID bundle).

needs: For real receipts: two hosts without egress, the published verifier release; expected verdicts taken from a reference run, fixed before the isolated runs. The service verifier behind an API cannot be the system under test for 'no network'; this vector targets the distributed verifier.

subcases.construction: bundle A-a, run on each of two isolated hosts
subcases.T_derivation: T = nTime(h*) of the fixture's own receipt proof and headers (a_sig and receipt_anchor as stamped; rows 11.1-11.4 pass); U = 7200 + max nTime(h*..h*+5) (A10.1.1)

sequence.setup: two hosts, fresh installs of the same verifier release, network interfaces down or egress denied (verify with a failed outbound probe before and after)
sequence.pass: every step's six stable fields and utc_assessment equal its fixture's expected.json; H1 and H2 agree byte-for-byte on the six fields
